topics.title: Axle removal and replacement
topics.summary: Same sequence for 30 / 40 / 50 mm. DD2 adds the overload clutch and has **no RHS insert** (axle lives in the gearbox hollow shaft). Leave the DD2 engine bolted unless you are aligning a new build.

topics.title: Axles, rims and tyres
topics.summary: The rear axle is a cantilever spring. Stiffness (material + **ID^4**) controls how fast the inside rear lifts and returns. Hollow axles are lighter and springier than old solid Bambino bars.

topics.title: The braking system
topics.summary: Power cited: ~1.5 kW Bambino to ~24 kW DD2. All karts have a **rear disc**. Bigger karts add **two front discs** because brake dive unloads the rear and the fronts do most of the work.

topics.title: Caster and camber adjusters
topics.summary: Yoke hole axis sets **caster** (side view, off vertical) and **kingpin inclination**. Changing inclination changes **camber** (front view): negative = tops in, positive = tops out. Camber on karts is usually quoted in **mm**.

topics.title: Centrifugal clutch
topics.summary: Shoes or a slotted disc are thrown out against a **drum that freewheels on a needle bearing**. Force scales with mass and with **rpm²**.

topics.title: Chains, sprockets and ratios
topics.summary: Power sets top speed; **torque at the rear tyres** sets acceleration. Class engines are largely sealed; gearing is the legal torque lever.

topics.title: Changing tyres
topics.summary: Tools: compressor, gauge, **bead breaker**, tyre tongs, valve key, tyre grease or dishwashing liquid.

topics.title: Chassis cornering dynamics
topics.summary: Cornering is CG location, weight transfer, caster, and chassis stiffness (plus more).

topics.title: Chassis size vs axle choice
topics.summary: Standard paddock rule (true for most **1050 mm** seniors): mid-range axle; **stiff** for cold/slippery; **soft** for high grip / rubbered; high-power likes stiff; low-power and tall drivers like softer.

topics.title: Chassis straightening
topics.summary: Rubbing is racing until the tubes take a **permanent set**. Many bends are recoverable; a **kinked / creased** tube has lost strength — usually buy a new chassis. Do not cut-and-weld mystery tube (unknown alloy, heat-treat, HAZ).

topics.title: The Dellorto carburettor
topics.summary: Jobs: atomise fuel to a stable A/F, and meter mixture with the slide (or butterfly). Pump petrol ignites ~**7:1 to 20:1**; stoich **14.7:1 by mass** (~9000 L air per 1 L fuel). SA Rok OKJ uses Dellorto VHSH 30 (page also mentions VHST 24 BS

topics.title: Engine mixture flow
topics.summary: Path: airbox → carb → inlet → crankcase → transfers → burn → exhaust port → tuned pipe. Port **height** vs TDC/BDC is the timing.

topics.title: Eyeballing the temperatures
topics.summary: Temps are a tool for longevity, economy, or power — not a substitute for the stopwatch.

topics.title: Homologation insights
topics.summary: Tool numbers: [`data/sporting-msa.json`](../data/sporting-msa.json). FIA → CIK (karting, 1962) → ASN (MSA in ZA).

topics.title: The ignition system
topics.summary: Spark must fire **before TDC** so peak pressure lands just after TDC. More rpm → more crank angle in the same burn time → **more advance**. Analogue = fixed advance. Digital = rpm-mapped.

topics.title: Intro for rookies
topics.summary: Club process is similar everywhere. The ASN issues the rules. Register with the club and sign the indemnity before track time. Do a structured intro (circuit closed to others) before you spend heavily.

topics.title: Kart setup

topics.summary: Kart suits are **abrasion**, not fire. No harness/suspension → you get thrown around and may slide on asphalt.

topics.title: Substance abuse
topics.summary: In a kart, a changed reaction time is a **safety** problem for other drivers and marshals, not only a health problem for the user. Strict liability: whatever is in the system counts, intent does not.

topics.title: Tillotson HW-49A (OK-N)
topics.summary: OK-N uses a **diaphragm** carb with a **butterfly**, not a Dellorto slide. Pump + pump diaphragm + **metering diaphragm**. Works in any orientation (same family as a chainsaw carb).

topics.title: Tyre setup
topics.summary: Four contact patches about the size of a palm keep the kart on the road. Treat them as the primary sensor.
